transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. To answer your question directly: yes, running a microwave completely empty for 10 minutes is very likely to have caused damage. The microwaves need food or water to absorb the energy; without it, the heat builds up inside and can melt internal components or burn off plastic parts. Because there is an active burning hazard, please do not use the appliance again until a qualified engineer has checked it. To help identify what might be wrong, with the microwave unplugged, could you look at the right-hand wall inside for a small, flat rectangular cover (usually white or cream)? Please let me know if that cover looks burnt, holed, or warped.

It's only turned off at the switch, still plugged in. I'll leave it for now. There was a burnt electrical smell and some smoke from the side vents when we opened the door. I can see a brownish mark on the panel on the side wall, but I'm not sure if that's the cover you mean. Is it safe to keep, or should I bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The smoke and burnt smell confirm that components have been damaged. Please unplug the appliance immediately at the socket. Do not attempt to use it again, even for a short test, as this could cause a fire or electrical fault. Because the damage is internal and involves high-voltage components, you should contact the manufacturer's support line or a qualified appliance engineer for an inspection. They will need to replace the burnt waveguide cover or other damaged parts before it can be used safely again.
